pr.title: Return 404 when search yields no results

behavioralChanges.summary: Empty search results now return HTTP 404 instead of HTTP 200 with an empty list.
behavioralChanges.before:
GET /search?q=unknown → 200 OK, body: { "results": [] }

search() always returns { status: 200, body: { results } } regardless of whether results is empty.
behavioralChanges.after:
GET /search?q=unknown → 404 Not Found, body: { "error": "No results found" }

search() would return status 404 when results array is empty.

sources.note: Baseline search() function — always returns status: 200. The proposed change would branch here to return 404 when results.length === 0.
SearchResponse interface only permits status: 200. The type must be widened to allow 404 before the change can compile.
Task description confirming the proposed response-code change.

behavioralChanges.summary: The client empty-state display path changes: it must now handle a 404 response rather than checking for an empty array.
behavioralChanges.before: interpretResponse() checks response.body.results.length === 0 to decide whether to return { kind: 'empty' }.
behavioralChanges.after: interpretResponse() must detect a 404-status response (and its { error } body) to return { kind: 'empty' }, since the 200 path will no longer carry an empty results array.

sources.note: interpretResponse() currently assumes status 200 always and branches only on results.length. This logic breaks when the service returns 404.
Import of SearchResponse type — currently typed as status: 200 only. Must be updated to accept the new 404 variant.
Compatibility note explicitly identifies interpretResponse() and the SearchResponse type as the two client-side touch points.

behavioralChanges.summary: Existing unit tests that assert status: 200 on a no-results query will fail after the change.
behavioralChanges.before: searchService.test.ts asserts response.status === 200 for 'zzz-no-match'. searchClient.test.ts constructs SearchResponse with status: 200 and an empty results array.
behavioralChanges.after: These tests must be updated: the service test should assert status 404, and the client test must supply a 404-shaped response for the empty-state case.

sources.note: Directly asserts status 200 for a no-match query — will fail if service returns 404.
Asserts empty results array on 200 response — test shape becomes invalid after the change.
Constructs a SearchResponse with { status: 200, body: { results: [] } } — this response shape will no longer be emitted by the service.

reviewLocations.label: searchService.ts — SearchResponse type and search() return branch
reviewLocations.reason: The type must be widened from status: 200 only to a union including 404, and the search() function needs a conditional return for the empty-results case. These are the two lines of code that define the entire contract change.

source.note: Covers both the SearchResponse interface (lines 16-19) and the search() function body (lines 41-56).

reviewLocations.label: searchClient.ts — interpretResponse() and SearchResponse import
reviewLocations.reason: interpretResponse() must be updated to branch on status rather than results.length. The imported SearchResponse type must also accept the 404 variant. If this is not updated, the client will either silently mishandle 404 as a 'results' state or fail a TypeScript compile.

source.note: Import (line 9) and interpretResponse() function (lines 24-29) are both affected.

reviewLocations.label: searchService.test.ts — no-results status assertion
reviewLocations.reason: Line 7 asserts status 200 for a no-match query. This test will fail after the change and must be updated to assert 404. It is also the place to add a test for the new error body shape.

source.note: Two tests covering the no-results path; both become invalid after the change.

reviewLocations.label: searchClient.test.ts — empty-state fixture
reviewLocations.reason: The empty-state test constructs a { status: 200, body: { results: [] } } fixture. After the change the service no longer produces this shape for empty results; the fixture must be replaced with a 404-shaped response.

source.note: interpretResponse empty-state test — fixture shape becomes stale.

decisions.question: Is HTTP 404 the right status code for a valid query that returns zero results?
decisions.context: REST conventions differ: 200 + empty list means the collection exists but has no matching items; 404 means no resource was found. The compatibility note flags this as an open question requiring explicit team agreement.
decisions.stakes: If 404 is chosen, all current and future clients must distinguish 'empty results' from 'server error'. Caching layers may treat 404 differently from 200. If another team later adopts 200 + empty list as the standard, this endpoint will be a special case.

sources.note: Explicit call-out that this decision needs team agreement before implementation.

decisions.question: Should a blank or whitespace-only query also return 404, or remain 200 + empty?
decisions.context: The current search() function treats a blank query as a special case that returns an empty list (line 44-45 of searchService.ts). The proposed change description mentions only 'no results found' — it is unclear whether a blank query is covered by the same 404 rule.
decisions.stakes: If blank queries return 404, clients that use blank queries as a 'show nothing' initial state will break. If they remain 200 + empty, there are now two empty-result shapes, which complicates client logic.

sources.note: Blank query is handled by q.length === 0 check — an explicit early-return path distinct from the filter producing zero results.
Existing test asserts empty list for blank query — would need updating if blank queries also return 404.
